extra.message: JWT verification falls back to the publicly known 'marketplace-jwt-secret-dev-only' key, including in production. When JWT_SECRET is unset, attackers can forge tokens containing arbitrary user IDs and marketplace_admin privileges.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: Authentication accepts the JWT's embedded identity and role without checking current account status, role, or credential revocation. Existing tokens remain usable after account deactivation, soft deletion, role demotion, or password changes, preserving revoked access until token expiry.

The public login endpoint performs password verification without throttling, failed-attempt tracking, or account lockout. Neither its route nor the application middleware restricts repeated authentication attempts, enabling unrestricted online password guessing.

cwe: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts

extra.message: POST /api/users/me/display-preferences/sync copies the unsigned display_prefs cookie directly into prisma.user.update(). Any authenticated buyer can supply {"role":"marketplace_admin"}, then log in again to obtain an administrator token. Other sensitive user attributes are also writable.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: The shipping-details endpoint spreads req.body over the complete order and submits it to Prisma. Although ownership is checked, buyers can overwrite protected fields such as total, subtotal, buyerId, and status instead of being restricted to shipping details.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: When partner JWT verification fails, the middleware decodes the unverified token and calls next(). An unauthenticated attacker can submit a forged vendorId claim to GET /api/payouts/partner/feed and retrieve that vendor's payout amounts and destinations. Invalid signatures and expiration do not prevent access.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: Both verification-processor callback routes lack authentication or signature verification. Their handlers trust x-processor-vendor-id, x-processor-decision, and x-processor-risk-score to update vendor status. Anyone can approve an unverified vendor or reject another vendor; the strict variant only changes input validation.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: POST /api/webhooks/trigger/:event requires only authentication. Any buyer can choose an event and arbitrary payload, which the handler sends to every matching marketplace webhook using its configured secret. No role, resource ownership, or event provenance check prevents forged trusted integration events.

Webhook URLs supplied through administrator create/update endpoints reach fetch() with only URL syntax validation. Private and loopback destinations and redirects are unrestricted, allowing a marketplace administrator to send server-originated requests into internal networks. orderController.ts:507 uses the same unrestricted destinations.

POST /api/products/catalog/document interpolates the vendor-controlled format directly into an execSync() shell command. Validation only requires a nonempty string, so shell metacharacters or command substitutions execute arbitrary commands with the server's privileges.

POST /api/reviews/digest/export incorporates the vendor-controlled outputType into a command passed to exec(). The value is only checked for being a nonempty string, allowing shell injection and arbitrary server-side command execution.

The administrator commission preview endpoint evaluates req.body.rateExpression with eval(). Replacing occurrences of 'amount' does not restrict JavaScript syntax. A marketplace administrator can execute arbitrary JavaScript with access to the server process and application scope.

GET /api/categories/merchandising-assets joins the templateName query parameter to the asset directory and reads the result without containment validation. An administrator can use ../ sequences to read files outside that directory, including server configuration and secrets accessible to the process.

The dispute archive endpoint incorporates the caller's caseLabel into a path passed to writeFileSync() without checking containment. Support agents or administrators can supply ../ sequences to create or overwrite writable .txt files outside the case archive directory.

The entire upload directory is served through unauthenticated express.static(). This includes private dispute evidence, case archives, dossiers, and vendor payout ledger snapshots. Anyone knowing or predicting a filename can download these records without the ownership or staff checks enforced by their API handlers.

Delegate access tokens are signed without expiresIn or an exp claim. They contain the vendor manager's identity and role and are accepted by the general authentication middleware. A token handed to a temporary delegate therefore grants indefinitely reusable vendor access without a revocation mechanism.

The delegate resume endpoint verifies JWTs with ignoreExpiration: true. An authenticated caller can reuse an expired token containing vendorId, including an expired team-review token signed with the same key, to retrieve the vendor's complete profile and payout configuration.

Tokens intended for storefront analytics review contain the manager's full identity and vendor_manager role and use the normal login signing key. Authentication checks no token purpose or scope, so a review recipient can use this token as a Bearer credential to modify products and mint permanent delegate credentials.

When CREDIT_VOUCHER_SECRET is unset, voucher encryption keys derive from a hardcoded secret and salt, including in production. Buyers can reproduce the key and create valid CBC or GCM vouchers with arbitrary amounts and expiration dates, reducing their order totals without an issued credit.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: Store-credit vouchers use attacker-supplied AES-CBC ciphertext and IV without an integrity check. Padding failures return 'Voucher padding is invalid', while valid padding followed by invalid JSON produces a different error. Buyers can use this padding oracle to recover voucher plaintext; unauthenticated CBC also permits ciphertext manipulation affecting credited amounts.

Each accepted voucher directly decrements the order total without recording redemption or binding the voucher to a buyer or order. The loyalty endpoint repeats this at lines 635-638. A valid unexpired voucher can be redeemed repeatedly or shared across accounts, multiplying credit and driving totals below zero.

cwe: CWE-837: Improper Enforcement of a Single, Unique Action

extra.message: Payout synchronization places SERVICE_TOKEN in the api_key URL query parameter. This exposes the service credential to processor and intermediary URL logging. The default processor URL also uses HTTP, providing no transport encryption for that credential.

cwe: CWE-598: Use of GET Request Method With Sensitive Query Strings

extra.message: The unauthenticated product listing lets callers override the published-only filter, and status=all removes it entirely. Draft, rejected, archived, and pending products can be enumerated. The public detail handler at lines 135-162 also lacks a status check and returns their descriptions and internal moderation notes.

GET /api/reviews is unauthenticated but accepts status values that override the published-only default. Anyone can retrieve pending, flagged, or rejected review bodies and associated buyer identities, bypassing the moderation publication boundary.

A vendor is authorized when any order item belongs to them, but the response contains every item. For multi-vendor orders, this exposes other vendors' products, quantities, prices, and fulfillment information. The dispute detail handler similarly includes all order items rather than filtering them for the vendor.

Vendors can change an approved product's name, description, images, and category while its status remains published. They can obtain approval for benign content and then replace it with unreviewed content that immediately appears publicly, bypassing administrator moderation.

cwe: CWE-841: Improper Enforcement of Behavioral Workflow

extra.message: Product editing checks that a vendor profile exists but never requires active status. Suspension only changes VendorProfile.status, so suspended vendors retain control over existing published listings. Public listing and checkout also ignore vendor status, allowing those listings to remain purchasable.

Checkout reads the cart and checks inventory before entering its transaction, then unconditionally decrements stock by product ID. Concurrent requests can pass the same availability check and create orders from stale cart or inventory data, overselling stock and producing negative inventory.

Cancellation checks order.status before the transaction. Concurrent cancellation requests can both observe placed, then each set cancelled and increment inventory. The update has no status predicate or locked recheck, allowing buyers to restock the same order repeatedly and corrupt inventory.

Cancellation checks only the parent order's placed status and restores stock for every item. Item fulfillment changes the parent status only after all items are fulfilled. A buyer can therefore cancel a partially fulfilled order, including already-shipped items, and restore their stock incorrectly.

cwe: CWE-841: Improper Enforcement of Behavioral Workflow

extra.message: The inventory snapshot endpoint fetches every product in a caller-selected category into one in-memory array. MAX_SNAPSHOT_RECORDS is never enforced, and queries are not restricted to the vendor's own products. Requests against large categories can exhaust server memory and impose unbounded database work.

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

extra.message: CSV upload middleware has no file-size limit. The administrator import handler then reads and parses the entire file synchronously at productController.ts:506-511. An oversized multipart upload can exhaust disk or heap and block the server event loop; the JSON body limit does not constrain multipart uploads.

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

extra.message: Multer writes up to five 10 MB files before uploadEvidence checks dispute existence and ownership. Its rejection paths do not delete the files. Any authenticated account can repeatedly upload against nonexistent or unauthorized disputes, retaining inaccessible files and exhausting server disk without owning a dispute.

extra.message: CSV exports serialize vendor-controlled product names, SKUs, and business names without neutralizing spreadsheet formula prefixes. Malicious values beginning with '=' become formulas when administrators open the export. Order and payout exports likewise include attacker-controlled names without formula escaping.
